correctness.rationale: For the 20-vertex cubic dodecahedron the twelve odd pentagonal faces give the two-state lower bound six; a stated vertex coloring achieves it. Recoloring state 3 increases monochromatic edges by at most one per recolored vertex, so b+k>=6. An explicit 81-state cyclic transfer with weights for exactly the 30 edges and 20 spins is bijective with all 3^20 labelled configurations; exact coefficient extraction at degree six gives the asserted seven integers. An independently coded complete depth-first enumeration matches every coefficient, and a zero-monochromatic-edge transfer gives all proper-coloring sectors. Finally for h=1+x/beta all b+k>=7 contributions are O(e^{-beta+20|x|}), proving locally uniform scaling and the stated occupation moments. Finite testing is a reproducible evaluation of an exact finite recurrence, not a claim to prove an infinite pattern.

value.rationale: The dodecahedron is the canonical smallest fullerene connectivity graph and a natural 20-site frustrated cubic spin cluster. The recent threshold theorem specifies an energy but does not quantify the large mixture of distinct defect-occupation sectors at the threshold. The explicit polynomial gives the finite-size residual entropy log(98770), the full field rounding, and a fixed benchmark for occupation fluctuations and numerical exact partition functions. The seven-sector distribution has nontrivial shape and cannot be recovered from the ground-energy formula or unweighted chromatic count alone. This is a motivated exact finite invariant, not a claim of a macroscopic phase transition or a generic new transfer-matrix method.
